Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Authenticated RTC rendezvous primitives

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

A room code is a routing identifier, not proof of authority. rendezvous_code derives a 64-character code from the authenticated view's room, content, epoch and owner identity. rendezvous_proof signs a fixed 116-byte create/join request with the member's provisioned key and a signaling connection's challenge.

rendezvous_verify runs beside the native authority Service. It checks the MAC, connection challenge, current live grant, exact process incarnation and enabled membership. Only the current owner can create the authority's room; another registered member may join it. A changed content/epoch/owner produces a different room code. A stale grant, wrong challenge, tampered proof or non-owner creation request fails. Verification does not renew a lease or mutate durable records.

The signaling service must issue a fresh cryptographic challenge per connection, expire it and consume it once. Passing a reused challenge to this stateless verifier would not implement replay protection. The Godot frontend implements that lifecycle and connects it to RTC authorization. Public deployment/provisioning remains separate from the verified loopback fixtures.
